name: Statement & Argument
shortcutSummary: A strong argument directly relates to the statement topic, gives a definitive reason (not vague), and does not make universal or emotional claims.
conceptExplanation: Statement and Argument questions present a statement/policy and arguments for or against it. You must judge each argument as Strong (directly relevant, factual, important) or Weak (vague, emotional, irrelevant, or makes sweeping generalizations).

subtopics.name: Statement & Argument — Core Concepts
subtopics.explanation: Statement and Argument questions present a statement/policy and arguments for or against it. You must judge each argument as Strong (directly relevant, factual, important) or Weak (vague, emotional, irrelevant, or makes sweeping generalizations).
shortcuts: Relevance Test: Does the argument directly address the topic of the statement?
Definiteness Test: Strong arguments are specific and factual, not vague ("may", "perhaps" = weak).
Universal Statement = Weak: "All people think..." or "Everyone knows..." are typically weak arguments.
